expectation: Membrane rings on scattered small lymphocytes: CD8 intraepithelial cells sitting between gut epithelial cells, plus resident T cells and some dendritic cells in the lamina propria. A minority of cells, distinct dots and rings against a dark background.
observed: A: yellow haze over all tissue and the slide background; muscle layers and folds glow. B: fibrous haze, no cells. C: bright rim at a crypt lumen, not single cells. D: blurry blobs. E: speckle, only partly on CD8a; CD8a itself blotchy.
why: The signal follows tissue texture, autofluorescence and the crypt lumen border, with no distinct ringed lymphocytes in the epithelium; row E does not rescue it.
notes: CD103 shows as haze over the whole tissue and slide, brightest in muscle and along the crypt-lumen border, with no clear ringed intraepithelial lymphocytes. The CD8a partner is blotchy too, so row E is weak evidence.
